response: Reports of mechanical dysfunction in chronic oro-facial pain are indeed related to somatisation. Research suggests that self-reported mechanical factors associated with chronic oro-facial pain are confounded by psychological factors and are equally common across other frequently unexplained syndromes, indicating that they may represent another feature of somatisation. This implies that the use of extensive invasive therapy, such as occlusal adjustments and surgery, to change mechanical factors may not be justified in many cases, as the underlying issue may be more closely related to psychological factors rather than mechanical dysfunction.
